# StudyReels AI Pro

**The study app that shows its work.** Turn your class notes into short-form study reels — generated by Claude, personalized by a real recommender, and checked by a deterministic Trust Score that catches AI hallucinations before you study something wrong.

---

## The problem

Every EdTech app trying to compete with TikTok/Instagram scroll habits makes the same bet: wrap studying in a short-form video skin and hope it sticks. Almost none of them ask the harder question — if an AI is generating what a student studies, how do you know it isn't making things up?

StudyReels does both: it hijacks the scroll habit, and it's honest about its own AI.

## What it does

- **Notes → reels.** Paste real class notes, get a vertical feed of study reels (POV-style hooks, AI-narrated footage, avatar-led explainers), each with a plain-language concept breakdown and an active-recall quiz — generated by Claude directly from what you uploaded.
- **Trust Score.** Every generated reel is checked against your own source notes by a fully deterministic, rule-based engine — no second AI model quietly vouching for the first one. It flags numbers/claims that don't trace back to your notes, verifies the quiz's correct answer is actually grounded, and shows exactly which terms matched. Tap the 🛡️ badge on any reel to see the full breakdown.
- **Personalized feed.** A recommender model reranks your feed based on real interaction signals (watch time, likes, quiz accuracy) — the more you use it, the more it fits how you actually study.
- **Study Partners.** Get matched with classmates by shared classes/curriculum, send reels directly to friends, and ask an always-available AI Study Buddy to explain anything you're stuck on.

## Why it's different

Most "responsible AI" features in hackathon projects are a confidence percentage slapped on top of generated content — a number the model itself made up. The **Trust Score engine is not another model**. It's plain, inspectable logic:

1. Tokenizes the generated reel and the source notes
2. Computes what percentage of key terms in the reel are actually present in the notes
3. Flags any number/statistic in the reel that doesn't appear anywhere in the source
4. Checks that the quiz's correct answer is traceable to the notes, not invented

Every point in the score maps to a rule you can read in `server.js` — nothing is a black box grading another black box. It even scores our own local fallback template honestly (usually lower), because a trust signal that can't fail isn't a trust signal.

## Tech stack

| Layer | Tech |
|---|---|
| Frontend | React (in-browser Babel), Tailwind CSS — single-page app |
| Backend | Node.js, Express |
| Reel generation | Claude API (Anthropic) — script, description, and quiz in one call |
| Trust Score | Custom deterministic rules engine (no external model) |
| Recommender | Logistic regression, trained in Colab, exported as weights and run as plain JS at runtime |
| AI Footage clips | Pre-generated with Pictory AI (script-to-video with narration) |

## Architecture notes

- **One server, one URL.** Express serves the React frontend statically — `npm start` and you're done, no separate frontend/backend processes.
- **No live Python dependency.** The recommender is trained offline in a Colab notebook (`ml/studyreels_recommender_training.ipynb`) and the resulting weights are hardcoded into `server.js` as plain math. This means zero risk of a Python service dying mid-demo.
- **Graceful degradation.** If no Claude API key is configured (or a request fails), reel generation falls back to a local template rather than breaking the app — the Trust Score engine still runs on fallback content too.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env
# paste your real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY into .env
npm start
```
Open **http://localhost:5000** — frontend and backend on one port.

To see the pre-made AI Footage video reel, drop `cellular_respiration.mp4` into `public/videos/` (see `public/videos/README.md`).

### Demo accounts
All use password `password123`: `student`, `maya`, `jordan`. These auto-accept friend requests instantly, so you can demo the Study Partners / reel-sharing flow solo, without needing a second browser session.

## Honest limitations

- The recommender is trained on **simulated** interaction data (see the Colab notebook), not real logged student behavior yet — it's designed to be retrained on real activity as the app grows.
- AI Footage reels are **pre-generated** with an external tool (Pictory AI), not produced live by the app on each upload.
- Data storage is in-memory for this build (resets on server restart) — no persistent database yet.

We'd rather state these plainly than have a judge discover them first.
